title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.13895v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models reuse the same attention heads across tasks, but identifying these shared heads does not explain what they do differently in each task. A natural source of inspiration is task-dependent interactions among shared brain regions, which motivate a network view of language-model computation. Here, we compare fixed model components across tasks using identical graph facts, statements specifying which directed connections are present. We measure how interventions affect attention heads and the activation state in later layers (influence), as well as the answer (importance). Task changes redistribute the influence in five open-weight models spanning four families and 1.5-14 billion parameters. In Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-14B, an activation edit changes an early internal activation vector and switches which fact the model reads while the written instruction stays fixed. translated_title: 任务上下文塑造语言模型组件的角色
translated_abstract: 大语言模型在不同任务中会复用相同的注意力头，但仅仅识别出这些共享的注意力头并不能解释它们在每个任务中究竟做了什么不同的事情。一个自然的灵感来源是共享脑区之间随任务变化的相互作用，这启发了将语言模型计算视为网络的观点。在本文中，我们使用相同的图事实（即指明存在哪些有向连接的陈述语句）来比较不同任务下固定的模型组件。我们测量了干预对注意力头及后续层激活状态的影响（影响力），以及对答案的影响（重要性）。研究发现，任务变化会在五个开源权重模型（涵盖四个模型系列、参数规模从15亿到140亿）中重新分配影响力。在Gemma-2-9B和Qwen3-14B中，对早期内部激活向量进行编辑，可以在书面指令保持不变的情况下切换模型所读取的事实。随后，相同的注意力头会响应不同的图事实……
tldr: 该论文揭示了任务上下文会重新分配语言模型中共享注意力头的影响力，表明同一模型组件在不同任务中扮演着不同的功能性角色。
en_tdlr: Task context redistributes the influence of shared attention heads in language models, demonstrating that identical model components play different functional roles across tasks.
